$yvettes="Yvette's">> <</if>> <<set $story = "custom03">> <<goto "customisation">> <</linkreplace>> <<elseif $story is "custom03">>\ There are three skills in the game: physicality, intelligence and charisma. You're proficient at one, average at another and poor at the last of them. Physicality is your ability to intimidate, to outrun, to fight and to parkour. Intelligence is your ability to memorise, to see connections, to find solutions and shortcuts. Charisma is your ability to sweet-talk, to charm, to convince and gather sympathy. Every skill can get you out of, on the receiving end of or delivering a spanking. Every challenge you face in the game is rated from 1 and 10, where the higher number represents a more difficult challenge. To determine if you overcome the challenge a random number generator will select your effort. Most of the time you will be offered at least two alternative methods of tackling the challenge. Your worst skill will be a random number between 1 and 6. Your medium skill will be a random number between 3 and 8. Your best skill will be a random number between 5 and 10. Obviously, this means there might be some challenges you can't pass unless you're good at it and some you can't fail unless you're bad at it. The difficulty of some challenges will vary depending on your previous choices. Hopefully, this might increase replayability. You can save wherever you like but you //can't// backtrack, so I hope every challenge will feel like it has risk and consequence.<<if $best is $average or $best is $worst or $average is $worst>> class="pl-svg-title">FREEPORT PALMA</text> <text x="340" y="108" text-anchor="middle" class="pl-svg-sub">A SPANKING ADVENTURE</text> <line x1="310" y1="125" x2="370" y2="125" stroke="#c8102e" "The museum," $name voted with a shrug. "Mall means spending money I'm not sure I have yet. <<if $events.includes("arrivedbytaxi")>>I'm probably already over budget for the weekend since I caught a taxi here yesterday.<<elseif $events.includes("arrivedbybus")>>I had to take the bus, even with all my luggage when I got here yesterday.<<else>>I even walked all the way uphill from the docks yesterday, dragging all my luggage with me!<</if>>" $name admitted sheepishly. "Museum," Kali agreed sullenly. "Sure. Culture. Not like I haven't been there a thousand times with school or anything." $dani looked quietly relieved. Jessica nodded. Kali made a small sound that was not quite a sigh. "Maybe you could, you know, show and tell? We only just got here." $dani suggested. Kali shrugged, giving in. They set off after breakfast, heading along the curve of the island rather than down, the streets narrowing as they moved toward the older part of the city. The buildings here were different: heavier, older stonework, more elaborate, windows with deep sills and no particular logic to their arrangement. A red cat watched them from a wall and did not move. The Palmland Natural History Museum occupied what had once been, apparently, something else entirely. The building was too large and irregular to have ever been a home. Now its facade was a patchwork of different eras that had been added without ever quite agreeing with each other. A banner above the entrance read: //ONGOING EXHIBITION: THE ISLAND IN DEEP TIME//. "That banner has been there my entire lifetime." Kali remarked dryly, emphasising her point that the museum was old news to her. The entrance hall was cool and dim and smelled of old wood and something mineral. The reception desk was staffed by a single attendant who handed over a map without being asked and said: "Take your time. Most people don't see everything." $dani looked at the map. "There are six floors." "Most people," the attendant repeated, pleasantly. <<linkreplace "Look around">><<set $story = "museum01">><<goto "museum">><</linkreplace>> <<elseif $story is "museum01">>\ The first floor was given over to the natural world of the island itself. The centrepiece was a full-scale reconstruction of a Palmus Palma tree, its canopy spreading almost to the ceiling and far out in every direction. $name walked around it slowly. The leaves were unmistakable: broad and flat, each one divided into five lobes that spread from a central point, eerily like an open hand. Probably hundreds of them, reaching outward in every direction, pale green and slightly waxy under the museum's lighting. "That's where the name comes from," said $dani, reading from the exhibit panel. "//Palma//, from the old latin word for palm of the hand. The island was named for the tree." <<if $events.includes("seenpamphlet")>>"I read about it on the ferry," $name almost whispered, before <</if>>Kali interjected. "Back when the island was discovered, it was a base of operations for pirates. A Freeport. So for a few centuries, it was named 'Freeport Palma'. Almost impossible to find." "There's more here." $dani moved along the panel. "The sap. It says the leaves produce a resin that accumulates in the lower stems. Used for centuries by the islanders as a topical treatment for damaged skin, burns, soreness. The pharmaceutical industry has been trying to synthesise it for decades." $uShe paused. "It says they haven't managed it yet." "Of course they haven't," said Kali, with the particular tone of an islander for whom this was not news. "And the Palmus Palma won't grow anywhere else." The rest of the floor was botanical: specimens, pressed samples, cross-sections. There was an alcove dedicated to the island's fungi, which were numerous and, in some cases, bioluminescent. Jessica spent longer there than anywhere else, saying nothing. "That's really cool!" $name pointed at the exhibit. Jessica shrugged. "Cool. You mean interesting?
